name: 61 Cygni B

boundTo.source: El-Badry, Rix & Heintz (2021, MNRAS 506, 2269) list 61 Cygni A and 61 Cygni B in their Gaia EDR3 wide-binary catalogue (VizieR J/MNRAS/506/2269, source_id 1872046609345556480 and 1872046574983497216), 110 AU apart on the sky, with a chance-alignment probability of 4.1e-9: the pair is bound. This record adopts no orbit of the pair, so the star is placed by its own astrometry and carries no orbit.

description: A nearby orange dwarf, 60% of the Sun's width: its disc was measured by interferometry.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 820B: radius in solar radii, 0.601 +/- 0.0072, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 820B: mass 0.629 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 820B: effective temperature in K, 3932 +/- 25, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists

text.card: A nearby orange dwarf whose disc was measured by interferometry: 60% of the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Interferometry gives it 0.601 solar radii; with its total light, that makes its surface 3,932 K.
